title: How many socks guarantee a pair?

probes.question: How many people guarantee that at least two share a birthday?
True or false: if you pull 3 socks from a drawer of only black and blue socks, two of them must match.

image.alt: A tall wooden cabinet with hundreds of small pigeonhole slots, used for sorting hotel mail.

body.question: A drawer holds a mix of black and blue socks and you pull them out in the dark. How many must you pull to be certain of a matching pair?
body.reveal: Three. With two colours there are only two 'pigeonholes', so by the third sock one colour must repeat. This is the pigeonhole principle: more items than boxes forces a box to hold two. The same idea says 367 people guarantee a shared birthday.
